summary: The episode centers on NASA's detection of a massive subsurface Kelvin wave in the Pacific, signaling a likely moderate-to-strong El Niño in 2026 that could reshape global weather patterns. Major geopolitical shocks include a double earthquake in Venezuela killing 188, an Iranian projectile striking a commercial ship in the Strait of Hormuz, and power losses in Russian-occupied Ukraine. Economic updates show cooling US inflation (PCE at 2.6%), rising bond yields, and a risk-off stock rotation hitting tech stocks like Nvidia and Apple. In science, new studies link extreme heat to mental health emergencies, while engineers unveil self-regulating artificial photosynthesis and cryogenic neuromorphic chips. Tech business highlights include Samsung's $648 billion investment plan, IBM's sub-1nm chip tech, and massive funding rounds for AI agents Sierra ($950M) and testing firm Patronus AI ($50M). Cultural stories cover Mehdi Hasan's brief X suspension, Harvey Weinstein's dropped charge, Paris's midday alcohol ban during a heatwave, and a study on civic kindness. Sports news features Giannis Antetokounmpo's trade to Miami and World Cup upsets by Ecuador and Ivory Coast.
